findings.reason: half the node's declared control is unfalsifiable, so §6 could be closed on a test that cannot fail on the code it changes.
findings.text: §6's done-when reads "A test that reads each skill's fast path fails if either still leads with `summary`", but reckon-roadmap's fast path is the bare default call `roadmap(project="<project>")` (~/.claude/skills/reckon-roadmap/SKILL.md:18) with the word `summary` nowhere in it, so a test reading that fast path passes identically on the base commit and after the change and can never fail; only reckon-status's fast path names a view (`read_plan(project, view="summary")`, ~/.claude/skills/reckon-status/SKILL.md:17), and that is a different tool's view which §6 does not touch

findings.reason: the measure can be satisfied by an instrument that sees nothing, so the node's whole verdict rests on an unproven count.
findings.text: §8's verdict arm "plan-HTML and pointer-file fallbacks per coordinator-day down by at least half against §1" is an absence-shaped measure and the only control §8 declares ("The census matches one transcript known to contain MCP calls", line 242) is applied to MCP calls, not to the Bash-fallback parsing the verdict reads; a broken or window-blind fallback parser reports zero fallbacks, which is the largest possible reduction and passes the gate

findings.reason: an undefined denominator lets the node pick the one that passes, and the before/after comparison is not reproducible without it.
findings.text: "fallbacks per coordinator-day" names a unit whose denominator the plan never defines: the evidence record records five sessions across three days (~/.claude and docs/evidence/archive/the-mcp-answers-the-question-asked-landed.html), and dividing §1's totals by three days, by five sessions, or by session-days gives answers that differ by a factor of five, so the "down by at least half" verdict moves with the choice

findings.reason: the node must know which before figure its verdict is measured against, and two candidates differ in whether §1's upper-bound regex counts or the census's own run sets the bar.
findings.text: §8 states "Its first run is over §1's window ... That run is the before figure, so the before and after figures come from one instrument", then sets the done-when's benchmark as "against §1" (line 240), whose figures the evidence record itself records as a different one-off instrument's regex counts; the section therefore asserts a one-instrument pair and then reads its verdict off a cross-instrument comparison

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the plans §1 and §6 cite exist (a-read-answers-inside-its-deadline.html with §45 at line 296 and §46 at line 300; a-project-reads-as-one-picture.html with §3, §4 and §7; every-plan-write-goes-through-edit-plan.html; the-crew-surface-is-one-tool-and-a-few-verbs.html), reckon/mcp_census.py exists and does count connection failures and storage-slow results as §8 claims, and the five transcripts §8 names are listed in the evidence record.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §6's declared negative control cannot fail for one of the two skills it names, and §8's reduction verdict has no control over the instrument arm it reads.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §1's census record is committed at docs/evidence/archive/the-mcp-answers-the-question-asked-landed.html (commit 8d6138532, 7,646 bytes, carrying the script, its inputs and its verbatim output), and each section's other evidence is its own node gate log rather than a scratch path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the only symbols the plan proposes are `why(ref)` and census counts named by what they measure; no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches a symbol or a comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §8's done-when benchmarks the after figure against §1's one-off counts while §8's mechanism text says the before and after figures come from one instrument.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each section names one deliverable (a size contract, a row shape, a `why(ref)` read, a parity check, the default brief, a cursor, a re-measured census); §8's instrument-versus-verdict split is raised under done_when rather than here.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — every `plan-section-depends-on` edge resolves to a node that exists (s4→a-project-reads-as-one-picture#s2,#s4; s5→#s4; s6→a-project#s7 + this plan #s2; s8→#s2..#s7), and the brief §6 returns is sourced from a-project-reads-as-one-picture §7 (docs/plans/a-project-reads-as-one-picture.html:201), whose payload is a-project §2–§5; the earlier wiring-1 edge question is answered by the cited source, which carries a `reason` field and explicitly not `why` (a-project-reads-as-one-picture.html:118).
